quote: So we're not tied with them specifically, but we do work with Pacific Power to set up the system and connect it to the meter.
stewart_read: This is a credit, not a miss: the customer opened with a legitimacy/affiliation question and the rep answered with honest specificity, which is the correct pattern per protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number's 'specificity reduces suspicion' principle even though the trigger phrase differs slightly (affiliation vs. number source).
coaching_implication: Reinforce this instinct with the rep — naming the actual mechanism (works with Pacific Power to interconnect) is exactly the kind of specific, confidence-building answer that should be the template for other legitimacy questions.

quote: That's how do you make your money?
stewart_read: This is the first ask of a financial-mechanism question that belongs to the closer; the rep chose to answer it himself rather than bridge immediately, opening the door to two more rounds of the same question.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive engagement is also possible if the rep felt the customer would hang up without some answer, but the rep had the scope-hold language available and used it later (04:33), showing he knew the correct move and simply didn't deploy it here.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the escape hatch ('that's exactly what the specialist will walk you through') on the very first financial-mechanism question, not the third.

quote: Okay. So that break even, how how do you make money?
stewart_read: Second occurrence of the same unresolved question; the rep repeats nearly identical content ('we just sell you the system... that's where we make our money') instead of recognizing the pattern and redirecting to the specialist.
coaching_implication: When a customer asks the same question a second time in different words, that repetition itself is the signal to stop explaining and bridge to the closer — the rep should be trained to recognize the repeat, not just the content.

quote: I will be honest with you, Richard. I'm only in the scheduling department, so I don't need with the financial aspect of things.
stewart_read: This is the correct move, arriving on the third pass of the same objection rather than the first — a reactive fallback deployed only after the rep had already tried and failed twice to explain the financial mechanism himself, not a deliberately sequenced strategy.
alternative_hypothesis: A strategic read would hold if the rep had used the first two explanations to build rapport before pivoting; but the customer's response ('I think you're gonna end up wasting your time with me') shows the two prior explanations eroded confidence rather than building it, undercutting the strategic hypothesis.
coaching_implication: Show the rep the full arc from 02:42 to 04:33: the scope-hold line he used correctly at the end should be the opening response to the first financial question, not the third.

quote: I I gotta tell you. I'm not I mean, I, you know, I I don't know where you're calling from, but I live in Astoria, and it's overcast most of the time.
stewart_read: Customer raises a location/climate-based skepticism objection ('overcast most of the time... no one has solar here', continued at 02:09) that maps to an invertible pattern (what's costly is staying on the current bill regardless of sun exposure), but the rep responds with 'Fair enough' and repeats the generic bill-swap pitch instead of using the objection as a redirect.
coaching_implication: Coach a specific inversion for climate objections: acknowledge the weather concern briefly, then pivot to 'that's exactly the kind of site-specific factor the design team checks before you'd ever pay anything' rather than repeating the same bill-swap line verbatim.

quote: Yeah. Yeah. It it never turns into free.
stewart_read: Customer voices a prior-experience-driven skepticism that free offers always convert to a cost — this doesn't match any single scripted rebuttal (it's closer to an unscripted 'hidden costs anxiety' pattern than the price-estimate-before-design flow, which addresses ballpark pricing requests, not skepticism about the free-estimate claim itself) and represents a schema gap Ion hasn't yet documented.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: this is a recurring skepticism type not covered by the current rebuttals library (see schema section C5, hidden_costs_anxiety) and would benefit from an Ion-specific scripted response distinguishing free-estimate skepticism from ballpark-pricing requests.

quote: I think you're gonna end up, wasting your time with me. So you you might wanna move on to your next name
stewart_read: This is a soft, self-deprecating decline roughly 4:44 into the call, well past the first_30_seconds_only window that scopes protocols.hello_objection_not_interested, so no existing protocol directly covers it — it is a schema gap rather than a misapplied existing rule. The rep's response (free-estimate reframe at 04:58) was an attempt to re-engage but not a structured handling of this specific 'don't waste your time' framing.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read is also defensible: the rep simply had no scripted move for a late-call soft decline and improvised the free-estimate save, which is a reasonable ad hoc response given no schema coverage exists for this exact trigger.
coaching_implication: Flag for Kenny: the schema's hello_objection protocol only covers the opening 30 seconds; a parallel late-call 'let me move on to the next name' soft-decline pattern needs its own documented response, since this call shows the free-estimate reframe alone did not recover it.

quote: I I don't wanna go through with this. So, you know, you should just move on.
stewart_read: The call ends without the rep attempting any fallback — no callback offer, no text follow-up, no 'can I check back in a few weeks' close. The rep simply lets the decline stand.
coaching_implication: Coach a standard soft-close-on-decline move: even a firm 'no' can end with 'no problem, I'll leave the estimate open in case you change your mind' rather than ending the call with nothing captured.
